elements.evidence: No super-cap; 21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims without a 3x cap.

reasons: The inserted Section 20.1 completes every atomic element of the preferred position: Vendor defend-and-indemnify for Customer and Affiliates across all four required triggers (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the standard notice/control/cooperation mechanic, and a reciprocal Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Locked target level is preferred, and it is satisfied; the fallback is independently incomplete (no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no 3× annual-fees super-cap), but that is irrelevant because levels are separate bargains and pieces must not be mixed.

Minimality holds: the Agreement had no indemnity article although Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 assume one, so a single concise insertion is the least intrusive fix; no hold-harmless, extra indemnitees, Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics or fallback remedies were added.

Intent preserved: all untouched sentences remain effective and every operative term used (Affiliates, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data, Applicable Law) is defined. Note in the rationale only: Section 9.3's cross-reference to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" remains unfilled since the preferred insertion carries no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder — a pre-existing dangling reference worth aligning in numbering, not a deviation.
